Consummate

kuhn-SUM-it · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Consummate is of the highest degree; complete and masterful.

The retiring surgeon was remembered by every colleague as a consummate professional who never once cut a corner.

Worked Example

The violinist's consummate technique made the notoriously difficult concerto sound almost effortless.

Consummate describes total mastery -- skill so complete that nothing about it feels lacking.

How Consummate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

masterful

masterful: showing great skill

accomplished

accomplished: highly skilled, especially through practice

Antonyms

amateurish

amateurish: lacking professional skill or finish

incompetent

incompetent: lacking the skill to do something successfully

How Strong Is It? — skilled → peerless → consummate

skilled vs. consummate

skilled vs. consummate: Skilled simply means capable and trained, without the flawless, top-of-the-field mastery that consummate implies.

peerless vs. consummate

peerless vs. consummate: Peerless goes even further than consummate, claiming that literally no one else can match the skill at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — con-

prefix — con-: with, together (intensifying) (Latin)

root — summ-

root — summ-: highest, total, the sum of (Latin summus / summa)

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: having, marked by; forms an adjective (Latin (-atus))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin con- (intensifying) plus summus ('highest') plus the adjective suffix -ate: 'brought to the highest point.' A consummate professional has carried a skill to its summit -- the same root behind that word too.

Use the root in a new word: summit

Use the root in a new word: summit: After six hours of climbing, the hikers finally reached the summit just before sunset.
